CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Billy is a 74-year-old patient presenting with a cough that started approximately one week ago. He reports productive cough with yellow sputum. He states he has been feeling worse over the last two days. Patient reports subjective feeling of warmth but denies taking his temperature. He denies chills. He reports general achiness at times but denies shortness of breath. He also reports nasal congestion with postnasal drainage and mild sinus pressure. No other household members are sick. Additionally, patient reports that while coughing earlier today, he fell down approximately 4-5 stairs and twisted his right knee. He is able to walk but has a mild limp. Right knee pain is primarily on the medial aspect and does not feel like it will give out. Patient has been taking over-the-counter Dayquil which has helped minimally with symptoms. He denies taking any pain medication for the knee injury.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Respiratory: Productive cough with yellow sputum. Denies shortness of breath.
Constitutional: Subjective feeling of warmth. General achiness. Denies chills.
ENT: Nasal congestion with postnasal drainage. Sinus pressure.
Other: Right knee pain from fall.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension (diagnosed and managed over the past year)
Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
Over-the-counter Dayquil as needed

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Occupation: Teacher
Living situation: Lives with wife
Other: Sports fan

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood Pressure 125/62, Heart Rate 80s, Oxygen Saturation 97% on room air
Head and Neck: Bilateral maxillary sinus tenderness to palpation. Nasal exam with erythema and edema of bilateral nasal turbinates with yellow discharge. Throat exam with midline uvula, no erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space. Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy noted.
Pulmonary: Coarse rhonchi bilaterally that clears with cough
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated
Right Knee: Pain to palpation, decreased flexion and extension, ecchymosis to right medial knee, no effusion

RESULTS
No laboratory results available at this time. Imaging and laboratory studies ordered (see plan).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Viral syndrome with mild bronchitis
Continue over-the-counter medications for symptomatic relief. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily to assist with expectoration of sputum. No antibiotics indicated at this time. Advised patient to call if symptoms worsen; chest x-ray may be considered at that time to rule out pneumonia.

2. Right medial collateral ligament strain (from fall this morning)
Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain and inflammation. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening exercises. Order right knee x-ray to rule out bony injury.

3. Hypertension
Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order lipid panel to assess cardiovascular risk. Discussed importance of diet modification and blood pressure monitoring.

4. Diabetes mellitus
Order hemoglobin A1c to assess glycemic control and determine if metformin adjustment needed. Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Counseled patient on importance of monitoring sugar intake and checking blood glucose levels. Advised to report blood sugar readings through patient portal.
